mainText:
If you only remember one thing today, remember this. Meta agreed to pay roughly seventeen billion dollars to settle state child safety claims. It is the largest settlement with a big tech company in history. And it comes with binding product changes, not just a cheque.

Section one. Meta's settlement is the story of the week. This came from your Tech Policy Press newsletter, plus N P R and C N N.

Meta settled a bloc of state child harm claims for about seventeen billion dollars. That's twelve billion paid over ten years. Plus another five billion, but only if YouTube, TikTok and Snap reach comparable deals and adopt the same changes.

The money is not the interesting part. The product changes are. Time limits. Nighttime access blocks. An age assurance framework. Parental controls on Instagram and Facebook. Tech Policy Press said it was a week where the lead paragraph wrote itself.

Why it matters. That contingent five billion is designed to drag the rest of the industry into the same rulebook, which makes this a de facto standard rather than a one company penalty.

Section two. Open A I is shutting off Cursor. This came from your A I News digest by swyx.

After Cursor was acquired by SpaceX, multiple model providers are ending their partnerships. Open A I plans to block Cursor users from reaching its models entirely. As swyx put it, the Elon versus Altman feud now has a real, shipping consequence.

Why it matters. If model access can be revoked over an ownership dispute, then every A I product built on somebody else's A P I is now carrying political risk on its balance sheet.

Section three. China's A I weekend. This came from your Recode China A I digest, covering August twenty third through the twenty ninth.

Z dot A I claimed the anonymous model that had been quietly topping leaderboards. They shipped G L M five point three Flash on August twenty sixth. DeepSeek is reportedly valued at seventy four billion dollars. And Beijing staged a robot olympics.

Elsewhere in Chinese releases this month: Alibaba's Qwen Image three point oh, and WAN three point oh, which generates thirty seconds of ten eighty p video, with audio, in a single pass.

Why it matters. The open weight frontier keeps moving east. And it's moving on a faster release cadence than the American labs.

Section four. A hundred companies warn about A I powered cyber attacks.

More than one hundred technology and security firms signed an open letter this week. That includes Open A I, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft. They're calling for coordinated defence against increasingly capable A I driven cyber threats. They named hospitals, water systems and internet infrastructure as the exposed surfaces.

Related, from your Information newsletter: the Hugging Face hack postmortem, which they describe as chilling.

Why it matters. Rivals rarely co sign anything. The joint letter is itself the signal about how fast offensive capability is compounding.

Section five. Chips. Enforcement is catching up with policy.

U S prosecutors charged three men with conspiring to smuggle about two and a half billion dollars of Supermicro servers, containing restricted Nvidia G P Us, to Chinese buyers. At least five hundred and ten million dollars of that hardware allegedly got through.

Meanwhile the old bipartisan consensus has fractured into a three way standoff. The White House is loosening controls on finished chips. Congress is trying to tighten them. And the chip industry is lobbying against both.

Why it matters. Export controls only work if enforcement scales with them. A two and a half billion dollar smuggling scheme suggests it hasn't yet.

Section six. Rules that are now actually in force.

The E U A I Act's transparency obligations took effect on August second. Chatbots must disclose that they are not human. A I generated or altered media must be labelled. Fines go up to fifteen million euros, or three percent of global turnover, whichever is higher. The tougher high risk obligations got pushed back to December twenty twenty seven.

California's A I Transparency Act, S B nine four two, also took effect August second. It covers generative A I services with more than a million monthly users in the state. And the F T C signalled it intends to enforce against A I enabled personalised pricing.

Why it matters. That's the top of the news. Your full briefing is in the recording.
